name: Silky Screw Set for GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy
title: Silky GomBoy Screw Set (PocketBoy, BigBoy)
h1: Silky GomBoy Screw Set (Fits PocketBoy and BigBoy)
meta: Silky GomBoy screw set: the replacement pivot hardware for GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy folding saws. When to replace it, how to fit it, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement pivot hardware to bring a loose Silky folding saw back to tight.
summary: The Silky GomBoy screw set is the replacement pivot hardware for Silky's GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy folding saws. If your blade wobbles, the lock feels vague, or the screw has gone missing on a job, this is the inexpensive fix that keeps a good saw in the pouch.
highlights: Replacement pivot screw hardware for Silky folding saws
Fits the GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy lines
Fixes blade wobble and lost hardware
Cheaper than replacing the handle
Worth keeping a spare set in the truck
specs: Silky GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy folding saws

p: A Silky folding saw pivots on a single screw and nut. Fold it open and closed a few hundred times a season, drop it out of a tree once or twice, and that hardware loosens, strips, or simply backs out. A blade with side play cuts crooked, binds in green wood, and puts more stress on the lock than it should.

This screw set replaces that pivot hardware on GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy saws. It is a small part, but it is the difference between a saw that tracks straight on a clean pruning cut and one that wanders and tears bark. Browse more pole saws, poles and kits if you are setting up a full pruning kit.
Silky handles and blades hold up for years, so the pivot hardware is often the first thing to give out. Replacing it costs far less than a new saw and keeps a familiar, broken-in handle in your kit.

Remove the blade, clean pitch and grit out of the handle, and fit the new screw and nut snug enough to remove play while still letting the blade fold freely. Check that the lock engages fully in the open position before you go back to work.

Confirm the set matches your specific model and blade size with the seller before ordering, since Silky has made these saws in several sizes over the years. Keep a spare set in the truck; it weighs nothing and saves a day of cutting with a loose saw.

faq.q: Will this fit every Silky folding saw?
faq.a: It is listed for the GomBoy, PocketBoy and BigBoy lines. Other Silky models may use different hardware, so confirm the fit for your exact saw before ordering.

faq.q: How do I know the pivot screw needs replacing?
faq.a: If the blade has side play when locked open, the screw will not hold tension, or the threads are stripped, replace the set rather than adding more torque.

name: Gasket Kit for Husqvarna T540XP
title: Husqvarna T540XP Gasket Kit: Fit, Uses and Price
meta: Husqvarna T540XP gasket kit for top-handle saw repairs: when gaskets cause air leaks and lean running, what to check during a rebuild, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement gaskets for servicing a Husqvarna T540XP top-handle saw.
summary: A Husqvarna T540XP gasket kit gives you the replacement gaskets you need when a top-handle saw is opened up for engine or carburetor work. Old gaskets that are torn or compressed can let in air, and an air leak makes a saw run lean, hot and unpredictable.
highlights: Replacement gaskets for the Husqvarna T540XP
Use when the engine or carburetor is opened for service
Helps prevent air leaks that cause lean running
Inexpensive insurance during any rebuild
Keeps a climbing saw reliable

body.h: When a T540XP needs new gaskets
p: The T540XP is a hard-working climbing saw, and top-handle saws get a lot of heat cycles, vibration and drops. Any time you pull the muffler, carburetor or cylinder, the old gaskets are compromised. Reusing them is a common cause of air leaks, and an air leak lets the engine run lean, which can lead to high idle, poor throttle response and, at worst, a scored piston.

A gasket kit puts fresh seals back into the saw so it holds the tune it was set to. If you are chasing a saw that will not idle or surges at the top end, a pressure and vacuum test is the right place to start before you replace parts.

Clean every mating surface completely, fit the gaskets dry unless the service manual says otherwise, and torque fasteners evenly. Confirm the kit contents match the job you are doing, since some kits cover only certain gaskets.
If you are not comfortable with engine work, have a qualified dealer handle it; a climbing saw needs to be dependable at height. Find more Husqvarna power equipment parts for the rest of the job.

While the saw is apart, it is a good time to check the fuel line, impulse line, intake boot and filter for cracks or hardening, since those also cause air leaks. Fixing everything at once saves opening the saw twice.

faq.q: Can I reuse the old gaskets on my T540XP?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Compressed or torn gaskets are a common source of air leaks, and new ones are inexpensive compared to engine damage.

faq.q: What are signs of an air leak?
faq.a: A high or hanging idle, surging, poor response to tuning, and a saw that runs hot are typical signs. A pressure and vacuum test confirms it.

name: Yale Beeline Lanyard with ISC Triple-Locking Snap
title: Yale Beeline Lanyard with ISC Triple-Locking Snap
h1: Yale Beeline Lanyard with ISC Triple-Locking Snap
meta: Yale Beeline lanyard with an ISC triple-locking snap for work positioning in the tree. How it is used, adjuster setup, inspection, and typical street price.
tagline: A rope positioning lanyard in Yale Beeline, finished with an ISC triple-locking snap.
summary: The Yale Beeline lanyard pairs Yale's Beeline rope with an ISC triple-locking snap for a supple, easy-handling positioning lanyard. It is a practical choice for climbers who want a rope lanyard for pruning and removals without wire-core stiffness.
highlights: Yale Beeline rope for good hand and hitch grip
ISC triple-locking snap on the working end
Rope lanyard for work positioning and pruning
Pairs with a friction hitch or mechanical adjuster
Lighter and easier to handle than a wire-core flipline

p: A rope lanyard is your second point of attachment when you are working a stem or spur climbing a removal. Choke it around the trunk or a limb, take up slack with the adjuster, and lean back to free both hands for the saw. Beeline is known for a firm, round hand that holds hitches well and runs smoothly through mechanical adjusters.

The ISC triple-locking snap closes on a saddle D-ring or bridge with a positive, three-step gate, so it does not roll open against hardware. Pair the lanyard with a friction hitch or a mechanical adjuster that is rated for the rope diameter. See more rope lanyards if you want a different length or connector.

Lanyard length decides how big a stem you can wrap and how much tail you manage. Longer lanyards reach around big trunks but leave more rope to handle on smaller wood, so pick a length that matches the trees you usually climb.

A rope lanyard will not stop a chainsaw, so keep the bar away from it and consider a wire-core flipline for heavy saw work around the lanyard. Check the rope for cuts, glazing and hard spots, and check the snap gate for full, crisp closure before each climb.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: Is a rope lanyard cut-resistant?
faq.a: No. A rope lanyard can be cut by a chainsaw. Many removal climbers use a wire-core flipline as a backup when making big cuts around their tie-in.

faq.q: What adjuster works with this lanyard?
faq.a: Use a friction hitch or mechanical adjuster that the manufacturer rates for the lanyard's rope diameter. Confirm compatibility before climbing.

name: Husqvarna Adjustable Friction Saver
title: Husqvarna Adjustable Friction Saver: Uses and Price
meta: Husqvarna adjustable friction saver for protecting bark and rope at your tie-in. How an adjustable saver sets and retrieves, plus inspection tips and price.
tagline: An adjustable rope friction saver that fits a range of limb sizes at the tie-in.
summary: The Husqvarna adjustable friction saver protects both your climbing line and the tree's cambium at the tie-in point. Because the length adjusts, one saver fits a wide range of limb and stem sizes, which makes it a handy everyday piece for MRS climbing.
highlights: Protects bark and cambium at the tie-in
Reduces wear and heat on your climbing line
Adjusts to fit a range of limb diameters
Ring-to-ring design for setting from the ground
Retrievable with the right technique
specs: Protecting bark and rope at the tie-in

body.h: Why use an adjustable friction saver
p: Running a climbing line straight over a limb chews bark, can damage the cambium, and adds friction that wears your rope and makes moving rope (MRS) climbing harder work. A friction saver gives the rope a clean metal surface to run over and keeps the rope off the bark.

The adjustable design lets you shorten or lengthen the saver to suit the limb, so the rings sit where they should and do not pinch together on a small union. That flexibility means you carry one saver instead of two or three fixed lengths. Compare other options in friction savers.

Pair the saver with a climbing line and hitch that are sized for its rings, and check that the rings let your hitch or knot pass through if you plan to retrieve it from the ground. A saver that will not release is a long climb back up.

Most climbers set a ring-to-ring saver from the ground with a throw line, then retrieve it the same way when they are done. Practice the setup on the ground before relying on it, and make sure the adjustment is set and secured before you load it.

Inspect the rope or webbing for cuts and abrasion and the rings for grooves before each use. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: Can I set this friction saver from the ground?
faq.a: Ring-to-ring friction savers are commonly set and retrieved from the ground with a throw line. Learn the method from a qualified trainer and practice before relying on it.

faq.q: Do I need a friction saver for SRS climbing?
faq.a: SRS anchors do not move rope over the limb the same way, but many climbers still use cambium savers or anchor slings to protect the tree and rope. Choose an anchor rated for the system.

name: DMM Revolver Rig Locksafe Carabiner
title: DMM Revolver Rig Locksafe Carabiner: Uses and Price
meta: DMM Revolver Rig Locksafe carabiner: an auto-locking biner with a built-in pulley wheel for redirects and mechanical advantage. Uses, care and typical price.
tagline: An auto-locking carabiner with a built-in pulley wheel for redirects and pulley systems.
summary: The DMM Revolver Rig is a Locksafe auto-locking carabiner with a pulley wheel built into the basket. It cuts friction where rope turns around the carabiner, which makes it useful for redirects, mechanical advantage systems and tidy climbing setups.
highlights: Integrated pulley wheel in the rope basket
Locksafe auto-locking gate
Reduces friction at redirects
Useful for building mechanical advantage
Saves carrying a separate small pulley

p: Every time rope turns around a plain carabiner, it loses energy to friction. The Revolver's wheel lets the rope roll instead of slide, so a redirect or a simple 3:1 haul system runs noticeably easier. Climbers use them on the bridge, at redirects in the canopy, and in light pulley systems for pulling tension or tensioning lines.

The Locksafe gate is DMM's auto-locking design: it closes and locks on its own, and opening it takes a deliberate sequence. That gives you a secure connection without having to remember to spin a screw gate. Browse more auto-locking carabiners for other shapes and materials.
Because the wheel is part of the carabiner, the setup stays compact on your saddle and there is one less piece of hardware to clip, lose or forget.

Load the carabiner along its major axis and keep the wheel side where the rope runs. Do not side-load it over a limb or across hardware. Rinse grit out of the wheel and gate after dirty jobs and let it dry.

Check that the gate snaps shut and locks fully every time. Retire any carabiner that has been dropped onto a hard surface from height or shows cracks or deep grooves. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: Is the Revolver Rig a replacement for a rigging block?
faq.a: No. It reduces friction in climbing and light pulley systems. For lowering wood, use a rigging block and hardware rated for the loads involved.

faq.q: What is a Locksafe gate?
faq.a: Locksafe is DMM's auto-locking gate. It locks automatically when it closes and needs a deliberate twist-and-pull to open.

name: Husqvarna 520iHT4 Battery Pole Hedge Trimmer (Bare Tool)
title: Husqvarna 520iHT4 Battery Pole Hedge Trimmer
h1: Husqvarna 520iHT4 Battery Pole Hedge Trimmer (Bare Tool)
meta: Husqvarna 520iHT4 battery pole hedge trimmer with an articulating head for tall and wide hedges. Who it suits, what the bare tool includes, and typical price.
tagline: A professional battery pole hedge trimmer with an adjustable cutting head.
summary: The Husqvarna 520iHT4 is a professional battery pole hedge trimmer with an articulating cutting head for reaching the tops and far sides of tall hedges. This listing is the bare tool, so you bring your own Husqvarna battery and charger.
highlights: Battery-powered pole hedge trimmer
Articulating head for tops and sides of tall hedges
Bare tool: battery and charger sold separately
Quiet enough for noise-sensitive properties
No mixing fuel or pulling a starter rope
specs: Pole hedge trimmer with articulating head
Bare tool (battery and charger sold separately)

p: Tall privacy hedges and long screen plantings are slow, tiring work from a ladder. A pole trimmer with an adjustable head lets you stand on the ground and cut the top flat, then angle the head to work the far face without moving the ladder every few feet. For crews that also do tree work, that means less time on ladders and fewer fall hazards.

Battery power suits residential and commercial properties with noise rules or early start times, and it removes fuel mixing and pull starts from the day. See other battery-powered equipment that runs on the same platform.

For tree crews, a pole hedge trimmer also handles low hedges and screen plantings around the drop zone, so a clean-up visit can include hedge work without a second crew or extra gas equipment on the truck.

The bare tool makes sense if you already run Husqvarna professional batteries in other tools. If not, budget for a battery and a charger, and match battery capacity to how many hours of trimming you do in a day. Check compatibility with the seller before ordering.
Wear eye and hearing protection, gloves, and keep a clear zone around the cutting head. Keep the blades clean and lubricated, and never reach toward the cutter while the battery is installed.

faq.q: Does the 520iHT4 come with a battery?
faq.a: No. This is the bare tool. The battery and charger are sold separately.

faq.q: Why choose an articulating head?
faq.a: An angled head lets you cut the top and far side of a tall hedge from the ground, which is faster and safer than repositioning a ladder.

name: Husqvarna Z560 Zero-Turn Mower
title: Husqvarna Z560 Zero-Turn Mower: Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna Z560 commercial zero-turn mower overview: who it suits, what to check on a used or new unit, routine maintenance, and the typical price range.
tagline: A commercial-grade Husqvarna zero-turn for crews that mow as well as cut trees.
summary: The Husqvarna Z560 is a commercial zero-turn mower from Husqvarna's professional line, built for crews that mow large properties day after day. For tree and landscape companies that also hold mowing contracts, it is the kind of machine that pays for itself on acreage.
highlights: Commercial-grade zero-turn mower
Built for daily professional use
Zero-turn steering for fast trimming around trees and beds
Dealer service network
Suits tree and landscape crews with mowing contracts

p: A zero-turn mower is a production tool. It turns in its own footprint, so you can cut tight around trunks, beds and obstacles and spend less time on trimmer cleanup. A commercial model like the Z560 is aimed at operators who put hundreds of hours a year on the machine and need a frame, deck and drive system that take that abuse.

Specifications such as engine model and deck width have changed between model years and configurations, so confirm the exact build with the dealer before you buy. Browse other power equipment for the rest of your fleet.

For crews that switch between tree work and maintenance contracts, a commercial mower keeps a steady stream of work moving through the slower months, and the same truck and trailer can often carry both setups.

On a used unit, check hours, deck condition, spindle bearings, belt wear and the hydrostatic drive response in both directions. Ask for service records. On a new unit, look at local dealer support, since uptime matters more than sticker price.

Keep blades sharp, grease spindles and pivots on schedule, and change engine and hydraulic oil at the intervals in the operator's manual. Use the rollover protection and seat belt as directed, take care on slopes, and keep people clear of the discharge.

faq.q: What deck size does the Z560 have?
faq.a: Deck options have varied by configuration and model year. Confirm the deck width and engine for the specific unit with the dealer or the serial number.

faq.q: Is a commercial zero-turn worth it for a tree company?
faq.a: If you hold regular mowing contracts, yes. If mowing is occasional, a lighter residential or entry commercial model usually makes more sense.

name: Husqvarna 522HDR75S 30 in Double-Sided Hedge Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 522HDR75S 30 in Hedge Trimmer
h1: Husqvarna 522HDR75S Professional 30 in Double-Sided Hedge Trimmer
meta: Husqvarna 522HDR75S professional hedge trimmer with a 30 in double-sided coarse-cut blade for heavy hedge work. Who it suits, care tips and typical price.
tagline: A gas professional hedge trimmer with a long, double-sided coarse-cut blade.
summary: The Husqvarna 522HDR75S is a professional gas hedge trimmer with a 30 in (75 cm) double-sided blade built for coarse cutting. It is made for crews that reduce overgrown hedges and thicker growth, not just trim fine shoots.
highlights: 30 in (75 cm) double-sided blade
Coarse-cut tooth spacing for thicker growth
Gas-powered for all-day work
Double-sided blade cuts on the push and pull
Professional-grade Husqvarna build

body.h: What coarse cut means on the job
p: Hedge trimmer blades come in fine and coarse tooth spacing. Fine spacing gives a neat finish on light growth. Coarse spacing opens wider so the blade can take thicker stems, which is what you want when you are cutting back a hedge that has been ignored for a season or two.

The long double-sided blade covers a lot of hedge face per pass and lets you cut in either direction, which speeds up wide flat tops. Compare it against other blowers and other equipment in the Husqvarna lineup.
Gas power suits crews that work far from a charger or run trimmers all day. Carry a spare can of mixed fuel so a big hedge job does not stop halfway because the tank ran dry.

Use fresh fuel mixed at the ratio in the operator's manual, or a pre-mixed fuel, and keep the air filter clean. Clean sap off the blades after each use and lubricate them so they do not gum up and bind.
A long blade is heavy at the end of a long day. Wear eye and hearing protection and gloves, keep a firm stance, and keep people clear of the work area. Stop the engine before clearing jams.
Sharpen or replace dull blades rather than forcing them through thick stems, which loads the gearbox and slows the job. A sharp coarse blade feeds itself into the hedge with little effort.

faq.q: Is a 30 in blade too long for small hedges?
faq.a: It can feel unwieldy on small, detailed shapes. It is best suited to long runs and tall, wide hedges where reach and coverage matter.

faq.q: What is the difference between coarse and fine cut?
faq.a: Coarse-cut blades have wider tooth spacing to take thicker stems. Fine-cut blades leave a neater finish on light, regular trimming.

name: DMM Stainless Steel Thimble
title: DMM Stainless Steel Thimble: Uses and Price
meta: DMM stainless steel thimble for protecting spliced rope eyes at hardware. Where arborists use a thimble, how to size one to your rope, and typical price.
tagline: A stainless thimble that protects a spliced eye where it bears on hardware.
summary: The DMM stainless steel thimble sits inside a spliced rope eye and protects it where it bears on a carabiner, shackle or ring. It keeps the eye open, spreads the load over a smooth radius and cuts down on abrasion at a high-wear point.
highlights: Stainless steel for corrosion resistance
Protects spliced eyes from abrasion
Keeps the eye open for clipping
Spreads load over a smooth radius
Useful in lanyards, slings and rigging lines

p: A soft eye on a rope sling or rigging line takes all its wear in one spot: where it wraps around the connector. Over time the fibers there flatten, glaze and abrade. A thimble gives the rope a hard, smooth bearing surface so the eye keeps its shape and the wear goes onto the steel instead of the rope.

Arborists see thimbles on rigging slings, lanyard ends and the eyes of lowering lines. They also make it easier to clip a carabiner into the eye because the opening never collapses. See more carabiners and hardware for related connectors.
Stainless steel suits rope that sees wet and muddy days, and it resists rust far better than plain steel. That matters on gear that lives in a damp truck bed or rope bag between jobs.

Thimbles are sized to rope diameter. Too small and the rope will not seat; too large and it can pull out of the eye. Confirm the thimble size against your rope with the seller, and have spliced eyes made by a qualified splicer to the rope maker's instructions.

Check thimbles for cracks, distortion and sharp edges, and retire any that are deformed. Use thimbled eyes only within the rated strength of the rope and hardware in the system, and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturers' instructions.

faq.q: Does a thimble increase rope strength?
faq.a: It mainly protects the eye from abrasion and crushing. Rated strength still depends on the rope, the splice and the hardware, so follow the manufacturers' ratings.

faq.q: Can I add a thimble to an existing eye splice?
faq.a: Usually the thimble is fitted when the eye is spliced. Ask a qualified splicer whether an existing eye can be adapted safely.

name: ISC Steel Offset Oval Carabiner
title: ISC Steel Offset Oval Carabiner: Uses and Price
meta: ISC steel offset oval carabiner for arborist climbing and rigging: why steel, why the offset oval shape, inspection tips and the typical street price.
tagline: A durable steel offset oval auto-locker for hard-wearing climbing and rigging setups.
summary: The ISC steel offset oval carabiner is a hard-wearing auto-locking connector for climbers and riggers who want steel's durability. The offset oval shape gives a wide gate opening while still keeping the load toward the spine.
highlights: Steel body resists wear from rope and hardware
Offset oval shape with a wide gate opening
Auto-locking gate
Good for pulleys, rigging hardware and high-wear spots
Made by ISC

p: Aluminum carabiners are light, but rope and steel hardware wear grooves into them over time. Steel carabiners last much longer in high-wear positions such as a pulley on the bridge, a rigging block attachment or a friction saver ring. The trade-off is weight, so many climbers carry steel where it counts and aluminum elsewhere.

The offset oval shape opens wide for clipping rings, D-rings and pulleys, and the curve helps keep the load near the spine where the carabiner is strongest. See other auto-locking carabiners for lighter or different-shaped options.

Steel also tolerates the occasional knock against hardware in the truck better than aluminum, and its extra weight is easy to live with in positions you rarely move, such as a pulley on your bridge or the attachment point on a friction saver.
Load the carabiner along its major axis with the gate fully closed and locked. Avoid cross-loading and loading over an edge. Clean grit out of the gate mechanism and keep it free of sap.

Before each climb, check that the gate snaps closed and locks every time, and look for cracks, corrosion and sharp grooves. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: Is a steel carabiner stronger than aluminum?
faq.a: Steel usually resists wear much better, and many steel carabiners carry higher ratings. Always check the rating marked on the carabiner for the job.

faq.q: Where should I use a steel carabiner?
faq.a: In high-wear spots, such as pulleys, friction savers and rigging hardware, where rope or metal contact would groove an aluminum carabiner.

name: Petzl Newton EasyFit Harness (International Version)
title: Petzl Newton EasyFit Harness, International Version
meta: Petzl Newton EasyFit fall arrest harness, international version: who it suits, how it differs from the ANSI version, fit and inspection tips, and price.
tagline: A full-body fall arrest harness designed to go on quickly and fit comfortably.
summary: The Petzl Newton EasyFit is a full-body fall arrest harness designed to be put on quickly, with a vest-style layout that keeps the straps from tangling. This is the international version, which is built to a different standard set than Petzl's ANSI-specific model.
highlights: Full-body fall arrest harness
Vest-style design for quick, tangle-free donning
Easy adjustment for a good fit
International version (check standards for your jobsite)
Suited to aerial lift and access work

body.h: Where a fall arrest harness fits in tree work
p: A tree climbing saddle is built for work positioning, but some jobs need fall arrest: bucket trucks and aerial lifts, rooftop access and some industrial sites. The Newton EasyFit is a full-body harness designed for that role. Its vest-style construction holds its shape, so you can put it on quickly without sorting out twisted straps.

The international version is built to standards used outside the US. Petzl also makes an ANSI version for North American markets. Check which standard your employer, client or regulator requires before you buy. See more fall protection for lanyards and other components.

For bucket truck work, the harness is used with a fall arrest lanyard and an anchor point approved by the lift manufacturer. Follow the lift maker's guidance on where and how to connect, and make sure everyone in the basket is trained on the system.

Adjust the leg loops and shoulder straps so the harness is snug, with the dorsal attachment between the shoulder blades. Connect only to anchors and lanyards rated for fall arrest, and use the attachment points as the manufacturer directs.

Inspect webbing, stitching and buckles before each use and retire the harness after any fall. Fall arrest equipment must meet the standards that apply to your jobsite and be used by trained workers following the manufacturer's instructions.
Store the harness clean and dry, away from chemicals and sunlight, and keep a written inspection record if your employer requires one.

faq.q: Can I climb trees in the Newton EasyFit?
faq.a: It is a fall arrest harness, not a tree climbing saddle. For climbing and work positioning in the tree, use a saddle designed for arborist work.

faq.q: What is the difference between the international and ANSI versions?
faq.a: They are certified to different standard sets. Choose the version that meets the standards required at your jobsite.

name: Teufelberger 10mm epiCORD Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
title: Teufelberger epiCORD 10mm Hitch Cord by the Foot
h1: Teufelberger epiCORD 10mm Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
meta: Teufelberger epiCORD 10mm hitch cord sold by the foot for tying friction hitches and prusiks. How to match it to your climbing line, care and price per foot.
tagline: Teufelberger hitch cord sold by the foot for friction hitches and eye-to-eyes.
summary: Teufelberger epiCORD is a hitch cord made for tying friction hitches, and this 10mm version is sold by the foot so you can cut exactly the length you need. It is a common choice for climbers who tie their own split tails and want a cord that grips and releases consistently.
highlights: 10 mm hitch cord
Sold by the foot
Made for friction hitches and split tails
Teufelberger build quality
Lets you cut lengths to suit your hitch

p: A friction hitch is only as good as the cord it is tied with. Hitch cord needs a cover that grips the climbing line, survives heat from long descents, and releases cleanly when you push the hitch. epiCORD is designed for exactly that job.

Buying by the foot lets you cut a split tail to suit your preferred hitch, whether that is a Distel, VT or a hitch you have tuned to your rope. Match the cord diameter to your climbing line: a 10 mm cord is commonly paired with lines around 11 to 13 mm, but always test on your own rope. Browse other tech cordage for alternatives.
Cutting your own also means you can keep a spare length in the truck and tie a fresh split tail on the job instead of waiting for a replacement.

Finish the ends with knots or terminations recommended by the manufacturer and learn the hitch from a qualified trainer. Test the hitch close to the ground before you climb on it, and adjust the number of wraps if it grabs too hard or slips.

Replace hitch cord when the cover is glazed, fuzzy, stiff or shows core. Hitch cord wears much faster than climbing line. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: How much hitch cord do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the hitch and your rope. Many climbers cut a little long, tie the hitch, and trim after testing. Ask a trainer for the length that suits your setup.

faq.q: Will 10 mm epiCORD work on my climbing line?
faq.a: It is commonly used on lines around 11 to 13 mm, but grip varies with rope construction. Test the hitch near the ground before relying on it.

name: Courant Koala V1.3 Climbing Harness
title: Courant Koala V1.3 Climbing Harness: Buying Guide
meta: Courant Koala V1.3 tree climbing harness: who it suits, how the bridge and back support feel on long climbs, fitting and inspection tips, and typical price.
tagline: A supportive European tree climbing harness for long days in the canopy.
summary: The Courant Koala is a tree climbing harness from French maker Courant, and the V1.3 is a later revision of the design. It is built for climbers who spend long hours suspended and want a supportive saddle with a bridge for free movement.
highlights: European-style tree climbing harness
Bridge attachment for free lateral movement
Supportive design for long suspended work
Gear loops and attachment points for tools
Made by Courant

p: European-style saddles like the Koala use a bridge as the main attachment, so your hitch or device can slide side to side as you work out a limb. That freedom of movement matters on big pruning jobs where you spend a lot of time at odd angles. The Koala's support is aimed at climbers who hang in the saddle for hours, not just a few quick climbs a week.
Fit is personal, and the best saddle is the one that suits your build and climbing style. Try one on if you can, and compare it against other European saddles.

Look at how the saddle carries a saw and handsaw, how the leg loops feel when you sit back for long periods, and how easily the bridge can be replaced. Those details matter more after a few hundred hours than the spec sheet does.

Adjust the waist and leg loops so the saddle sits snugly and the bridge rides at a comfortable height. Set up gear loops so your saw and handsaw do not hang where they swing into your legs. Replace the bridge at the interval Courant recommends or sooner if it shows wear.

Inspect webbing, stitching, buckles and the bridge before every climb, and retire the saddle if any part is damaged. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: What changed in the V1.3?
faq.a: V1.3 is a revision of the Koala design. Check Courant's current documentation for the specific changes and sizing.

faq.q: Is the Koala good for SRS climbing?
faq.a: Many climbers use bridge saddles for both MRS and SRS. Check that your chest harness and ascent setup are compatible with the saddle's attachment points.

name: Teufelberger drenaLINE 11.8mm Climbing Line
title: Teufelberger drenaLINE 11.8mm Climbing Line
meta: Teufelberger drenaLINE 11.8mm climbing line, a 24-strand arborist rope for MRS and SRS. How it handles with hitches and devices, care tips and typical price.
tagline: An 11.8 mm 24-strand climbing line from Teufelberger for everyday tree work.
summary: Teufelberger drenaLINE is an 11.8 mm 24-strand arborist climbing line built for everyday MRS and SRS work. It has a firm, round profile that holds hitches well and runs predictably through mechanical devices.
highlights: 11.8 mm diameter
24-strand cover construction
Works for MRS and SRS climbing
Firm, round hand for consistent hitch grip
Teufelberger quality control

p: An 11.8 mm line sits in the middle of the common arborist range, which means it works with most friction hitches and many mechanical devices rated for lines around that size. The 24-strand cover is tightly braided, so it resists picking up bark and sawdust and keeps a round shape under load.

That firm hand makes it predictable: your hitch grabs and releases the same way from the first climb of the day to the last. Always confirm that any mechanical device you use is rated by its maker for this diameter and construction. Browse more 24-strand climbing rope to compare.
Climbers who split time between pruning and removals often like a line in this size because it is easy to grip on long descents and holds up well to the extra wear of spar work.
Keep the rope in a bag away from fuel, bar oil, sharp tools and sunlight. Wash it gently as the manufacturer allows and let it dry out of direct sun. Never step on it or let it drag through grit.

Run the rope through your hands before each climb and look for cuts, glazing, flat spots and core showing. Retire it when in doubt. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.

faq.q: Can I use drenaLINE for SRS?
faq.a: Yes, it is used for both MRS and SRS. Make sure your SRS device is rated by its manufacturer for 11.8 mm, 24-strand rope.

faq.q: What hitch cord pairs with 11.8 mm rope?
faq.a: Many climbers use 8 to 10 mm hitch cord on lines around this size. Test the hitch near the ground before climbing on it.

name: SpiderJack 3 Replacement Parts
title: SpiderJack 3 Replacement Parts: What to Know
meta: SpiderJack 3 replacement parts for the ART mechanical friction device: which parts wear, when to replace them, inspection habits and typical part prices.
tagline: Manufacturer replacement parts to keep a SpiderJack 3 climbing device in service.
summary: SpiderJack 3 replacement parts let you swap worn components on ART's mechanical friction device for MRS climbing instead of retiring the whole unit. Wear parts are part of owning any device that rope runs through all day.
highlights: Replacement parts for the ART SpiderJack 3
Keeps a working device in service
Replace worn parts as the manufacturer directs
Cheaper than a new device
Use only genuine parts for the correct model

p: The SpiderJack 3 manages friction on a moving rope system with metal parts that the rope bears on all day. Rope carries grit and bark into the device, and over time that grinds down contact surfaces. Springs, pins and similar parts can also wear or get damaged in normal use.
ART designed the device to be maintained, so worn parts can be replaced rather than retiring the whole unit. Browse other MRS devices and accessories.

Keeping a spare of the parts that wear first in the truck can save a lost day if one fails inspection at the start of a climb. Ask the seller which parts ship together and which are sold individually.

Identify the exact part you need from the manufacturer's documentation and make sure it is for the SpiderJack 3, not an earlier version. Follow ART's instructions for replacement, and if the instructions say a part must be fitted by the manufacturer or a competent person, follow that.

After any repair, check the device function close to the ground before climbing on it. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user. Retire the device when ART's instructions say it is worn beyond service.
Clean the device as the manufacturer directs, especially after climbing on muddy or sappy rope, since grit speeds wear on every contact surface.

faq.q: Will SpiderJack 2 parts fit a SpiderJack 3?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Use only parts listed for your exact model and confirm the fit with the seller.

faq.q: Can I replace parts myself?
faq.a: Follow ART's instructions. Some parts are user-replaceable, while others may need a competent person or the manufacturer.

name: Weaver Rubberized Pole Saw Scabbard (BLT-105)
title: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard, Rubberized (BLT-105)
meta: Weaver pole saw scabbard in rubberized material for carrying a pole saw head safely on your saddle or in the truck. Fit, how climbers use it, care and price.
tagline: A rubberized scabbard to carry and protect a pole saw blade.
summary: The Weaver pole saw scabbard is a rubberized sheath for carrying a pole saw head safely on your saddle or in the truck. It protects the blade's teeth and protects you, your rope and your gear from them.
highlights: Rubberized construction for durability
Protects pole saw teeth and the climber
Carries on a saddle or in a truck
Weaver build quality
Model BLT-105

body.h: Why a pole saw needs a scabbard
p: A pole saw blade is long, sharp and easy to bump into rope, gear or your leg when it is hanging unprotected. A scabbard keeps the teeth covered when you are moving through the canopy, sending the saw up or down, or tossing it in the truck. It also keeps the teeth sharp longer by stopping them from hitting other tools.
Climbers often hang a pole saw scabbard from the saddle so the pole saw stays within reach while they work out a limb. Compare other pole saws and scabbards for different blade lengths.

A rubberized scabbard flexes instead of cracking when it gets knocked around, and it stands up to rain and sap better than fabric. That makes it a good fit for crews who carry pole saws on the truck every day.
Check that the scabbard length and opening suit your pole saw blade before ordering. A blade that is too long will stick out, and one that is too short may slide around.
Knock out sawdust and debris regularly so the blade seats fully, and check the attachment hardware for wear. Keep the scabbard away from your climbing line and lanyard.
When sending a pole saw up to a climber on a line, keep the blade in the scabbard until it is in reach, and agree on clear signals with the ground crew before you start.

faq.q: Will this fit my pole saw blade?
faq.a: Confirm the blade length and shape against the scabbard with the seller before ordering.

faq.q: Can I hang it from my saddle?
faq.a: Yes, many climbers carry a pole saw scabbard on the saddle. Attach it so the blade cannot swing into your rope or lanyard.

name: DMM Keanu Trolley
title: DMM Keanu Trolley: Speedline and Tensioned Line Use
meta: DMM Keanu trolley for tensioned lines and speedlines in tree work. How arborists use a trolley, how to set up a line safely, inspection and typical price.
tagline: A trolley pulley for moving loads or people along a tensioned line.
summary: The DMM Keanu trolley is a pulley built to run along a tensioned line, which makes it useful for speedlining brush and wood away from targets in tree work. It is designed to stay on the line while it moves.
highlights: Trolley pulley for tensioned lines
Useful for speedlining brush and wood
Designed to stay on the line while it runs
DMM build quality
Pairs with a rated carabiner

body.h: How trolleys help in tree work
p: When you cannot drop wood or brush, a speedline lets you send pieces along a tensioned line to a landing zone away from roofs, gardens and fences. A trolley rides that line and carries the load. A good one runs smoothly so loads do not stall halfway, and stays on the line so loads do not come off at the wrong moment.
The Keanu is designed for tensioned line work, so it is a better choice for speedlines than a standard rigging pulley that was never meant to travel. See more rigging pulleys for other jobs.
Speedlines also save time on jobs where wood would otherwise be lowered piece by piece into a cramped drop zone, because the ground crew can work the landing while the climber keeps cutting.

A speedline adds force to its anchors, so the anchor tree, the tensioning system and every component must be rated for the loads involved. Keep the landing zone clear and control the speed of loads with a tag or lowering line where needed.
Check the sheave turns freely and the side plates are not bent before each job. Plan speedlines with a qualified rigger and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
Use a separate trolley for each load in a busy system so the ground crew can unclip and return them without holding up the climber.

faq.q: Can I use a regular pulley on a speedline?
faq.a: A trolley designed for tensioned lines is a better choice. Standard rigging pulleys are not all designed to travel along a line.

faq.q: What connector should I use with the Keanu?
faq.a: Use a carabiner or connector rated for the load and compatible with the trolley's attachment point, per the manufacturer's instructions.

name: Distel Carbon 3 V 2020 Tree Gaffs with Click Buckles
title: Distel Carbon Spurs 3 V 2020 with Click Buckles
h1: Distel Carbon Spurs: Carbon 3 V 2020 Tree Gaffs with Click Buckles
meta: Distel carbon spurs, Carbon 3 V 2020 with click buckles: lightweight tree gaffs for removal climbers. How the buckles work, fit, care and typical price.
tagline: Lightweight carbon fiber climbing spurs with quick click-buckle straps.
summary: The Distel carbon spurs in the 3 V 2020 version use carbon fiber shanks to keep weight off your legs, and this model uses click buckles for fast, secure strap adjustment. They are aimed at removal climbers who spend long days on spurs.
highlights: Carbon fiber shanks for low weight
Click buckles for quick strapping on and off
Replaceable gaffs
Made by Distel in Germany
Aimed at full-time removal climbers

p: Every ounce on your lower legs gets lifted with every step up a stem. Over a full day of removals, lighter spurs mean less fatigue and better footwork when it matters. Carbon fiber shanks give Distel's climbers a stiff, light platform for that work.

This version uses click buckles instead of Velcro straps, so you can get into and out of the spurs quickly and get consistent tension. Compare it with other lightweight spurs to find the right fit and pad style for your legs.
Carbon spurs cost more than steel or aluminum models, so they make the most sense for climbers who spur every week. For occasional removals, a lighter aluminum spur is often the better value.

Spurs should sit snug on the boot and lower leg without pressing on your shin or ankle. Use the correct gaffs for the bark you climb and keep them sharpened to the manufacturer's profile. A dull gaff can cut out, which is dangerous.

Spurs are only for removals and emergency access, never for pruning live trees you are keeping. Inspect shanks, gaffs, straps and buckles before each climb. Always pair spurs with a lanyard and climbing line, and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
Keep spare gaffs and the gaff tightening hardware in the truck so a damaged gaff does not end a job.

faq.q: Click buckles or Velcro straps?
faq.a: Click buckles go on and off quickly with consistent tension. Velcro adjusts in finer steps. It comes down to personal preference and fit.

faq.q: Can I use these spurs for pruning?
faq.a: No. Spurs damage living trees. Use them only for removals or emergency access.

name: Husqvarna Pixel Chainsaw Bar 3/8 Mini x .043
title: Husqvarna 3/8 Mini Pixel Bar, .043 Gauge
meta: Husqvarna 3/8 mini pixel bar with .043 gauge for small and battery chainsaws. How to match bar, chain and sprocket, care tips and the typical price.
tagline: A narrow-gauge Husqvarna bar for small saws running 3/8 mini chain.
summary: The Husqvarna 3/8 mini pixel bar is a narrow .043-gauge guide bar for lighter saws that run 3/8 mini pitch chain. Narrow-gauge systems take a thin kerf, which helps small gas and battery saws cut faster for their power.
highlights: 3/8 mini pitch
.043 in narrow gauge
For lighter gas and battery saws
Thin kerf for efficient cutting
Husqvarna OEM bar

p: A guide bar has to match the chain's pitch and gauge, and the saw's drive sprocket and mount. This bar is set up for 3/8 mini pitch chain in .043 gauge, which is the kind of narrow system Husqvarna fits to lighter saws. Check the saw model, bar length and drive link count before ordering so everything lines up.

Narrow gauge means a thin kerf, so a small engine or battery motor spends less energy removing wood. That suits limbing, pruning cuts and storm cleanup. Compare other chainsaw bars for different lengths and pitches.
For climbers, a lighter bar on a small saw also makes the saw easier to handle one-handed in position and less tiring to carry on the saddle all day.

Flip the bar regularly to even out wear, clean the groove and oil holes, and dress the rails flat if they get burred. Make sure the saw is oiling properly; a dry bar wears fast and can pinch the chain.
Replace the bar if the rails are worn uneven, the groove is too shallow for the drive links, or the nose is damaged. Always wear chainsaw-rated PPE when running the saw.
Fit a new chain and check the drive sprocket when you put on a new bar, since a worn sprocket chews up a fresh bar and chain quickly.

faq.q: Will this bar fit my saw?
faq.a: Check the saw model, bar mount, length and drive link count against the bar's listing. Pitch and gauge must match your chain.

faq.q: Can I run .050 gauge chain on this bar?
faq.a: No. Chain gauge must match the bar groove. This bar takes .043 gauge chain.

name: Petzl Footape Adjustable Foot Sling
title: Petzl Footape Adjustable Foot Sling: Uses and Price
meta: Petzl Footape adjustable foot sling for rope ascent with a handled ascender. How climbers set the length, use it in SRS systems, inspect it, and typical price.
tagline: An adjustable webbing foot loop for ascending rope with a handled ascender.
summary: The Petzl Footape is an adjustable foot sling that clips to a handled ascender so you can stand up and push your weight up the rope. It is a simple, low-cost part of many SRS ascent setups.
highlights: Adjustable webbing foot loop
Pairs with a handled ascender
Quick length adjustment to suit your setup
Light and packs small
Made by Petzl

body.h: How the Footape fits an ascent system
p: In a basic rope-walking or frog-style ascent, a handled ascender on the rope carries a foot loop. You stand in the loop to push up, then sit back on your saddle-mounted device while you slide the handled ascender higher. The Footape is that foot loop, and its adjustment lets you set the length so each stroke is efficient.

Getting the length right is the difference between short, tiring steps and smooth progress. Set it on the ground, try a few strokes and adjust. See other foot ascenders and foot loops for more options.

Some climbers run two foot loops for a rope-walking style, while others use a single loop with a knee ascender or foot ascender. The Footape suits either layout as long as it is clipped to a compatible handled ascender.

The Footape is part of an ascent system, not a fall protection component on its own. Your life-support connection should always be your saddle-mounted device on a rated anchor. Check the webbing, stitching and buckle before each use, and replace the sling if it is cut, frayed or stiff.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.
Keep it out of chainsaw reach and away from fuel and bar oil in the truck.

faq.q: Can I use the Footape without a handled ascender?
faq.a: It is designed to clip to a handled ascender. Use it as the manufacturer directs.

faq.q: How long should I set the Footape?
faq.a: Set it so you get a comfortable, full step without overreaching. Test on the ground and adjust.

name: Sterling 10mm Flex Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
keyword: sterling flex eye to eye prusik
title: Sterling Flex Eye to Eye Prusik, 10mm Sewn
h1: Sterling Flex Eye to Eye Prusik, 10mm Sewn
meta: Sterling Flex eye to eye prusik, 10mm with sewn eyes, for friction hitches on MRS climbing lines. How to pair it with your rope, inspection tips and price.
tagline: A 10 mm sewn eye-to-eye hitch cord from Sterling for friction hitch climbing.
summary: The Sterling Flex eye to eye prusik is a 10 mm hitch cord with sewn terminations, ready to tie your friction hitch out of the bag. Sewn eyes are compact and low-profile, which leaves more cord for the hitch itself.
highlights: 10 mm hitch cord
Sewn eyes at both ends
Ready to tie: no knots to dress
Compact terminations save cord length
Made by Sterling Rope

p: An eye-to-eye is the heart of a traditional MRS climbing system: tie a Distel, VT or similar hitch on your climbing line, clip both eyes into a carabiner, and add a micro pulley to tend slack. Sewn eyes are smaller than spliced or knotted ends, so the hitch sits closer to the carabiner and you can use a shorter, more responsive cord.

Sterling's Flex cord is designed to grip and release smoothly. A 10 mm cord is commonly used on lines around 11 to 13 mm, but grip depends on rope construction, so test on your own line. Browse more eye-and-eye prusiks to compare.
Length matters too: a cord that is too short will not leave enough tails for a proper hitch, and one that is too long makes slack tending clumsy. Check the listed length against the hitch you tie.
Tie and dress the hitch close to the ground, load it, and confirm it grabs and releases before you climb. Adjust wraps or switch hitches if it slips or locks up.

Hitch cord is a wear item. Replace it when the cover is glazed, fuzzy or stiff, when the core shows, or when the stitching looks worn. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.
Keep a spare in your gear bag so a worn hitch never becomes a reason to keep climbing on it.

faq.q: Can I retie the eyes if they wear?
faq.a: No. Sewn eyes are factory terminations. Retire the cord when the stitching or eyes show wear.

faq.q: What rope does a 10 mm prusik work with?
faq.a: It is commonly paired with climbing lines around 11 to 13 mm. Always test the hitch on your own rope.

name: Weaver Velcro Cushion Wrap Pads
title: Weaver Climber Pads, Velcro Cushion Wrap
h1: Weaver Climber Pads: Velcro Cushion Wrap
meta: Weaver climber pads with cushioned Velcro wrap for more comfortable days on spurs. How wrap pads fit, when to replace worn pads, and typical street price.
tagline: Cushioned wrap pads that make spurs more comfortable on long removals.
summary: Weaver climber pads with a cushion wrap and Velcro closure spread spur pressure over more of your lower leg. They are an inexpensive upgrade for climbers whose shins take a beating on long removal days.
highlights: Cushioned wrap for lower-leg comfort
Velcro closure for easy adjustment
Spreads pressure from spur straps
Replaces worn or thin pads
Made by Weaver

p: Spurs transfer your weight through the shank into the strap and pad around your calf. Thin or worn pads concentrate that load, and after a full day of removals you feel it in your shins. A thicker, cushioned wrap pad spreads the pressure and keeps the spur from shifting on your leg.

Velcro wrap pads go on fast and adjust easily, which helps if you climb in different boots or pants. Check that the pads suit your spur's straps and rings before ordering. Browse more climber pads for other styles.

Pads also help the spur sit in the same place on your leg every time you strap in. A spur that rotates or slides under load is both tiring and less secure on the stem, especially when you cut in at an angle.
Brush out bark and sawdust after each use and let pads dry if they get wet. Replace pads when the cushion compresses flat, the Velcro stops holding, or the cover tears.
Pads are part of your spur system, so inspect them with your straps and gaffs before every climb. Spur only on removals and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
If your spurs still hurt with fresh pads, check the fit of the shanks to your leg length and the strap tension before assuming you need different spurs.

faq.q: Will these pads fit my spurs?
faq.a: Confirm compatibility with your spur model, straps and rings with the seller before ordering.

faq.q: How often should climber pads be replaced?
faq.a: When the padding is flattened, the closure no longer holds firmly, or the material is torn.

name: Marlow Raptor 16mm Rigging Rope
title: Marlow Raptor 16mm Rigging Rope: Uses and Price
meta: Marlow Raptor 16mm rigging rope for lowering wood in tree removals. What a 16mm line suits, matching blocks and devices, care, inspection and typical price.
tagline: A 16 mm rigging line from Marlow for lowering wood on removals.
summary: Marlow Raptor 16mm rigging rope is a lowering line for arborist rigging, sized for wood that is too heavy for light pruning lines. It suits crews running blocks and lowering devices on regular removal work.
highlights: 16 mm rigging rope
For lowering wood on removals
Pairs with blocks and lowering devices sized for it
Made by Marlow
A step up from light 1/2 in rigging lines

p: Rigging rope diameter follows the size of the wood you lower. A 16 mm line, around 5/8 in, is a common choice for crews lowering mid-size limbs and tops, where a light 1/2 in line would be pushed close to its limits. It is also a comfortable size to handle on a lowering device.

Match the line to your blocks, lowering device and slings: sheaves and bollards are rated for rope diameter ranges. Confirm the rated strength and construction with the seller and size the system with a safety factor for dynamic loads. Compare other rigging rope.

A heavier line also has more mass to absorb shock and more surface for wraps on a lowering device, which helps the ground crew control a piece with less effort. The trade-off is weight to carry and pull up into the tree.

Rigging lines take shock loads, heat from lowering devices and abrasion over bark. Inspect the rope after every job for cuts, glazing, crushed sections, and core showing. Retire it after a severe shock load or if you find damage.
Store rope in a bag away from fuel, oil and sunlight. Rig only within the rated strength of every component, and make sure the crew is trained under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
Keep a log of big catches and hard use so you know how much life the rope has left.

faq.q: Is 16 mm too big for my rigging block?
faq.a: Check the block's sheave rating. Blocks list the rope diameter range they are designed for.

faq.q: Can I use a rigging rope for climbing?
faq.a: No. Rigging rope is not designed or rated for life support. Use a rope made and rated for climbing.

name: Husqvarna Mini Accessory Carabiners (3-Pack)
title: Husqvarna Mini Carabiners, Accessory 3-Pack
meta: Husqvarna mini carabiners in a 3-pack for hanging small tools, keys and gear on a saddle or bag. Not for life support. Uses, limits and typical price.
tagline: Small accessory carabiners for organizing gear, not for life support.
summary: Husqvarna mini carabiners in a 3-pack are small accessory clips for organizing gear: hang a wrench, files, a bottle or keys on a saddle loop or gear bag. They are not rated for climbing or rigging and must never be used for life support.
highlights: Pack of three mini accessory carabiners
Handy for wrenches, files, keys and bottles
Organizes gear on saddles and bags
Not for climbing, rigging or fall protection
Husqvarna branding

p: Every climber ends up with small things that need a place: a scrench, a file, a water bottle, a phone lanyard or a set of truck keys. Mini accessory carabiners keep those items clipped to a saddle gear loop, a bag strap or a belt where you can find them.
Having a few spares also helps keep the gear in the truck organized. See other non-locking carabiners for more options.

A dedicated clip for small tools stops them from rattling around in a pocket or going missing in the leaves. On the ground, a mini carabiner on a bag strap keeps gloves, a radio pouch or a first-aid kit together.

Accessory carabiners are not climbing equipment. Never use them to connect a lanyard, a climbing system, a rigging component or fall protection, and do not use them to hang a chainsaw from your saddle.
Use only rated connectors for anything that supports a person or a load, and keep accessory clips visually separate from your life-support gear so nobody grabs the wrong one.
If the gate stops closing on its own or the clip bends, throw it away. They are cheap enough to replace, so there is no reason to keep a damaged one in service.

faq.q: Can I hang my chainsaw from one?
faq.a: No. Use a saw lanyard and a rated connector for your chainsaw.

faq.q: Are these carabiners rated?
faq.a: They are accessory clips and are not for life support, climbing or rigging.

name: Forester Rain Guard for Muffs and Screen
title: Forester Rain Guard for Earmuffs and Face Screen
h1: Forester Rain Guard for Muffs and Screen
meta: Forester rain guard for helmet earmuff and face screen setups. Keeps rain and debris off your face while you cut. How it fits, what it does, typical price.
tagline: A rain guard that helps keep rain and debris off your face screen.
summary: The Forester rain guard fits a helmet-mounted earmuff and face screen setup to help keep rain and falling debris off the screen. It is a small accessory that helps when you are cutting in wet weather.
highlights: Fits helmet earmuff and screen setups
Helps keep rain off the face screen
Sheds sawdust and debris
Light and low-profile
Forester brand
specs: Rain guard for muff and screen
Helmet-mounted earmuff and face screen systems (confirm compatibility)

p: Storm work and winter cutting often happen in the rain. Water running down a mesh or clear face screen blurs your view, and wet sawdust sticks to it. A rain guard sits above the screen and sheds most of that water and debris so you can see what the bar is doing.
It is a simple, inexpensive addition for anyone already running a helmet-mounted earmuff and screen. Browse other eye protection for screens and glasses.
Brims and rain guards also give a little shade, which helps reduce glare on a mesh screen when you are cutting into a low sun.
Confirm the guard is compatible with your helmet, muff and screen system before ordering. It should not block your view or stop the screen from lowering fully.
A face screen is not a replacement for safety glasses. Wear eye protection that meets the applicable standard under the screen, and inspect all helmet accessories for cracks and loose fittings.

Keep spare screens on hand. A guard keeps rain off, but a bent or clogged mesh still hurts your view and should be replaced. Clean the screen and guard with water, not solvents, which can damage plastics. Check the mounting clips each time you swap screens.

faq.q: Does this replace safety glasses?
faq.a: No. Wear rated safety glasses under a face screen.

faq.q: Will it fit my helmet?
faq.a: Check compatibility with your helmet, earmuffs and screen with the seller before ordering.

name: Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk Low-Friction Device
title: Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk Low-Friction Device
meta: Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk low-friction device for rigging points and redirects. How arborists use a low-friction ring, sizing to rope and slings, and price.
tagline: A machined low-friction device for rigging points and redirects.
summary: The Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk is a machined low-friction device that gives rope a smooth, fixed surface to run over at a rigging point or redirect. With no moving parts, it has nothing to seize or wash out.
highlights: Machined low-friction bearing surface
No moving parts
Builds a rigging point with a sling
Useful for redirects
Made by Tylaska

p: Low-friction devices sit between a plain ring and a pulley. Rope runs around a smooth, rounded machined surface rather than over a sheave. That gives more friction than a block, which can help control a light load, but much less than running rope over bark.

Arborists use them with a sling to build a rigging point, as a redirect for a lowering line, or in light lifting and tensioning systems. With no bearings or axle, they stand up well to dirt and wet. Compare other rings and rigging hardware.

The LFB-14 sits in the middle of the Basilisk range, so it is a practical size for light to moderate rigging on pruning and smaller removal jobs. Its machined finish means rope runs smoothly without the grabbing you get from a rough ring.
Tylaska makes the Basilisk in several sizes. Match the size to your rope diameter, sling and the loads you plan to put on it, and confirm the rated strength with the seller.

Inspect the bearing surface for grooves, burrs and cracks before each use. Rig only within the rated strength of every component in the system and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
Rinse it after muddy jobs and keep it with your slings so it is ready to go.

faq.q: Is a low-friction device better than a pulley?
faq.a: It is different. It adds a little more friction than a pulley, has no moving parts, and is compact. Choose based on the job.

faq.q: How do I pick a size?
faq.a: Match the device to your rope diameter, slings and expected loads, and check its rated strength.

name: Bag of Rope Ends
title: Bag of Rope Ends: Short Rope for Ground Use
meta: A bag of rope ends: mixed short lengths of rope and cord for tag lines, tying brush, practice knots and shop use. What to use them for, limits and price.
tagline: Mixed short rope and cord lengths for ground use, practice and shop jobs.
summary: A bag of rope ends is a mixed bundle of short rope and cord lengths left over from cutting rope to length. It is handy around the shop and on the ground for tying loads, practicing knots and hitches, and small jobs that do not need new rope.
highlights: Mixed short lengths of rope and cord
Useful for practice knots and hitches
Ties down brush, tarps and loads
Good value for shop and truck use
Not for climbing or rigging
specs: Not for life support or rigging

body.h: What rope ends are good for
p: When rope is cut from a reel to length, short tails are left over. A bag of those ends is useful in a lot of small ways: practicing friction hitches and knots on the ground, tying brush into a bundle, securing a tarp or a load in the truck, or making a quick tag line for a small piece.
Contents vary from bag to bag, so expect a mix of diameters, colors and constructions. Browse more tech cordage if you need a specific cord.

Rope ends are also handy for whipping practice, tying test splices, making a quick handle loop on a brush pile, or giving a new ground worker something to learn knots with during a break. Keeping a bag in the truck means nobody cuts a good rope for a small job.
Rope ends have unknown history and are not certified for any rated use. Never use them for climbing, rigging, lowering or anything that supports a person or a heavy load.
For training, they make great practice pieces. When it is time to climb on a hitch, tie it with new hitch cord rated for the job.
Mark them clearly or keep them in a separate bag from your climbing and rigging gear so they never get mixed in with rated rope.

faq.q: Can I use rope ends for prusiks?
faq.a: Only for practicing knots on the ground. Use new, rated hitch cord for climbing.

faq.q: What lengths are in the bag?
faq.a: Contents vary. Expect a mix of short lengths and diameters.

name: Petzl Secur Shoulder Straps for Positioning and Croll
title: Petzl Secur Shoulder Straps for Croll Setups
h1: Petzl Secur Shoulder Straps for Positioning and Croll
meta: Petzl Secur shoulder straps for holding a Croll chest ascender in position on a seat harness. How they set up for SRS ascent, fit, inspection and price.
tagline: Shoulder straps that hold a chest ascender in position for rope ascent.
summary: The Petzl Secur shoulder straps hold a chest ascender such as the Croll upright on your harness, so it runs smoothly as you ascend rope. They are a simple way to add a chest-mounted ascender to a compatible seat harness.
highlights: Shoulder straps for a chest ascender
Holds the Croll upright for smooth ascent
Adds an ascent setup to a compatible harness
Adjustable fit
Made by Petzl

body.h: Why shoulder straps matter for ascent
p: In a frog or rope-walking ascent, a chest ascender keeps the rope close to your body and grabs as you stand up in a foot loop. For it to work well, it needs to stay upright and tight. Shoulder straps hold it in place so the rope runs through cleanly instead of the ascender flopping forward.

The Secur straps are designed for Petzl's Croll and compatible harnesses. Check that your saddle has the attachment points the straps need before ordering. Browse more saddle parts and shoulder harnesses.

A good chest setup also makes rope ascent less tiring because more of each stroke goes into upward progress instead of pulling slack through a loose ascender. That matters on tall trees where you ascend a long way before working.

Adjust the straps so the ascender sits snug on your chest without pulling your saddle up. Shoulder straps are a positioning accessory: they keep the ascender in place, but your life-support connection remains your saddle and rated devices.

Inspect webbing, stitching and buckles before each climb and replace if worn or cut. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.
Practice the full ascent setup on the ground first.

faq.q: Will Secur straps work with my tree saddle?
faq.a: Only if your saddle has compatible attachment points. Check with the seller or Petzl's compatibility information.

faq.q: Are shoulder straps a fall arrest harness?
faq.a: No. They hold a chest ascender in position. They are not a fall arrest harness.

name: Dead Eye Ring Sling 1/2 in
title: Dead Eye Ring Sling 1/2 in: Rigging Uses and Price
meta: A 1/2 in dead eye ring sling for building rigging points and choking spars on removals. How it rigs, sizing for your wood, inspection tips and typical price.
tagline: A 1/2 in rope sling with a spliced eye and a ring for building rigging points.
summary: A dead eye ring sling in 1/2 in rope combines a spliced eye at one end and a ring at the other, so you can choke a stem and make a rigging point in seconds. It is a go-to piece for setting blocks and lowering lines where there is no good natural crotch.
highlights: 1/2 in rope body
Spliced dead eye at one end
Ring for choking and redirecting
Quick to set as a rigging point
Lighter choice for small to medium wood

body.h: How a dead-eye ring sling rigs
p: Wrap the sling around the stem, pass the dead eye through the ring, and cinch it down. The choke holds the sling in position on a vertical spar better than a basket, and the ring or eye becomes the anchor for a block, pulley or lowering line. Some crews also choke the piece with a ring sling and attach the lowering line to it.
The 1/2 in size is easy to carry and handle and suits small to medium wood. Check the length against the stems you work on. Browse more heavy-duty rigging slings for larger rope or longer slings.
Because the eye has no hardware, the sling is light and easy to throw over a limb or pass around a stem, and there is less metal to knock against the trunk when you set it.

Rate the sling against the dynamic load of the pieces you are cutting, not just their static weight, and confirm the sling's rated strength with the seller. Match it to the rest of the system, including the block and rope.

Inspect the rope for cut strands, glazing and stiff spots, the splice for slippage, and the ring for grooves or cracks. Rig only within the rated strength of every component and follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: What is a dead eye?
faq.a: A dead eye is a spliced loop at the end of the sling with no thimble or hardware, small enough to pass through the ring.

faq.q: Can I use a ring sling to choke the piece being cut?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the sling and ring are rated for the dynamic load of the piece.

name: 5/8 in Wire Core Positioning Flipline
title: 5/8 in Wire Core Flipline for Positioning
h1: 5/8 in Wire Core Flipline for Positioning
meta: A 5/8 in wire core flipline for work positioning on spar and removal climbs. Why wire core resists cuts, adjuster setup, inspection habits and typical price.
tagline: A 5/8 in wire core flipline for removal climbers working around a running saw.
summary: A 5/8 in wire core flipline gives removal climbers a positioning lanyard with a steel core that resists chainsaw cuts. It is the lanyard many climbers reach for when they are spurring a spar and making big cuts close to their tie-in.
highlights: 5/8 in diameter
Wire core resists chainsaw cuts
Positioning lanyard for spar and removal work
Pairs with a rated adjuster
Stiffer than rope lanyards for flipping around a stem

p: A rope lanyard can be cut by a running chainsaw in an instant. A wire core flipline has a steel cable inside the rope that resists an accidental cut, which buys real protection on removals where the bar is working close to your lanyard. The extra stiffness also helps the lanyard hold its loop when you flip it up a stem.
The 5/8 in size gives a full grip for flipping and is a common size for removal climbers. Compare other fliplines and lanyards for different lengths and adjusters.

The trade-off is weight and stiffness. A wire core flipline is heavier than a rope lanyard, and it is harder to tie a friction hitch on, so most climbers pair it with a mechanical adjuster rated for it.

Use an adjuster rated for the flipline's diameter and construction, and connect to your saddle with rated snaps or carabiners. Wire core is cut-resistant, not cut-proof, so keep the bar away from the lanyard.

Inspect the cover for cuts and the core for kinks, broken wires and corrosion, especially near the eyes. Retire the flipline after any saw contact that reaches the core. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb by a trained user.
Store it coiled loosely to avoid kinking the core.

faq.q: Is a wire core flipline cut-proof?
faq.a: No. It resists cuts but can still be damaged or cut. Keep the saw away from it and inspect it after any contact.

faq.q: Can I use a wire core flipline for pruning?
faq.a: It is heavy and stiff for pruning. Most climbers use a rope lanyard for pruning and save wire core for removals.

name: LogRite 12 in Milo Hand Log Tongs
title: LogRite Log Tongs: 12 in Milo Hand Tongs
h1: LogRite Log Tongs, 12 in Milo Hand Tongs
meta: LogRite log tongs, the 12 in Milo hand tongs, for lifting and dragging rounds and firewood without bending over. How they grip, sizing, care and price.
tagline: Hand log tongs for lifting and dragging rounds without straining your back.
summary: LogRite log tongs in the 12 in Milo size let you grab, lift and drag rounds and firewood without bending to grab them by hand. They save your back and your fingers when you are cleaning up a takedown.
highlights: Hand log tongs from LogRite
12 in size for rounds and firewood
Grab and drag without bending
Keeps hands away from pinch points
Simple, durable LogRite build

p: Cleaning up after a removal means moving a lot of wood. Picking up rounds by hand means bending over hundreds of times and putting fingers near pinch points. A pair of tongs grabs the round, lets you lift with your legs and a straight back, and drag pieces to the chipper, the truck or the stack.
The 12 in Milo is sized for rounds and firewood that one person can handle. Larger logs call for a cant hook, a log arch or a team. Browse more log handling tools for heavier work.

Tongs also help with splitting and stacking firewood, loading the truck, and moving rounds out of a client's yard. Anything that keeps your hands off wet, heavy wood cuts down on strains and pinched fingers by the end of the day.
Set the points into the wood, lift with your legs and keep the load close. Do not try to lift more than you can safely handle, and watch your footing on wet or uneven ground.
Keep the points sharp and clean, and check the pivot for looseness. Replace worn or bent parts before they let a round slip.
Hang them in the truck where they will not get buried under rope and saws.

faq.q: How big a log can the 12 in tongs grab?
faq.a: They are sized for rounds and firewood that fit in the jaws. Use a larger tool for big logs.

faq.q: Are log tongs worth it for tree crews?
faq.a: Yes. They speed up cleanup and reduce back strain and pinched fingers.
